idiom_name: Polly v8 retry strategy with DelayBackoffType.Exponential + UseJitter
implementation_notes: The schedule is configuration rather than code: ResiliencePipelineBuilder().AddRetry(new RetryStrategyOptions { BackoffType = DelayBackoffType.Exponential, UseJitter = true, Delay = base, MaxDelay = cap, MaxRetryAttempts = n }) performs classification, delay calculation and exhaustion, and from an HttpClient the standard resilience handler wires the same engine with documented defaults of 3 retries, exponential backoff, jitter enabled and a 2-second base delay inside a 30-second total timeout. With the exponential backoff type and jitter, Polly documents the randomization as a DecorrelatedJitterBackoffV2 formula rather than a fixed percentage, and DelayGenerator can override the calculation entirely - for example to honour a Retry-After header. The hand-rolled loop is only justified when the call site cannot take a Polly dependency.
pitfalls: The standard resilience handler already contains a retry strategy (and a circuit breaker, rate limiter and timeouts); adding another retry handler stacks two budgets with different schedules.
It retries every HTTP method by default: POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE must be excluded with DisableFor or DisableForUnsafeHttpMethods unless the operation is idempotent.

Delay is the base, not the interval: with exponential backoff and jitter the actual wait is computed per attempt, so MaxDelay and DelayGenerator interact and the realized delay can be lower than the previous one.
